    Import a wallet

    Paste a private key (WIF) or another wallet's 12 or 24 words; words give that wallet's first address. Kept here, encrypted; nothing is published.

    In a browser, the key goes through your tunnel to this arcade only. Do it on a computer you trust: browser extensions can read what a page shows.

    Receive

    ARCADE ID

    Paste or scan a code from a site: digiid:// signs you in to it (a key made for that one site), arcadesign:// lets it ask this app to sign (you approve each one here; your words never leave this app), arcadelink:// opens this account in a new browser. Check the site's name before you go on. ARCADE ID is built on Digi-ID, created by the DigiByte community.

    Sign in with a Dogecoin Arcade account

    Your account's words are kept on the arcade that holds your account, sealed under your password; any arcade hands out the sealed copy and only your password opens it, here on this PC. Your imported wallets, groups, address book and blocked list come with it. The password is not stored.

    Linked wallets

    Attach another wallet on this chain to your @tag. The wallet's key and your @tag's key both sign the link, so other arcades can check it. The key is kept here, encrypted.

    Your addresses on your profile

    List this wallet's own addresses (Pepecoin mainnet, Dogecoin and each other coin installed here) on your @tag's profile, so the Explorer shows them under your @tag. No private key is pasted: they come from your 12 words. It is one small transaction from your @tag's address; you see the fee first.

      Messages are sealed on the Pepecoin testnet chain to the other person's key, and a copy to yours, so they come back when you restore your 12 words. Each one is a transaction with a small fee; old Dogecoin Arcade accounts can read and reply.

      API

      For programs on this computer (sidecar apps)

      Chains & Coins

      Coins

      Install a chain to keep it on this arcade; nothing is installed unless you do it here. Coins you haven't installed can be borrowed through other arcades' Core nodes: this arcade keeps only their block headers and your own coins, and checks every block it reads. Installing a chain replaces its borrowed copy.

      Get it from

      Arcades on the mesh first: other V1.0 arcades' blocks, or an existing arcade's Core node. This waits up to a minute and a half for their answers, then uses the coin's own P2P network for anything left.

        Mine testnet

        Mines Pepecoin testnet blocks on this PC and pays your wallet. Mined coins can be spent after 240 blocks (about 4 hours).

          Options

          Your arcade account

          AccountAddressFrom

          The 12 words bring the whole account at once: its address on every chain (each chain's own, from the same words), its @handle and its coins, read back from the chains this arcade keeps. With no wallet here yet, they become this arcade's wallet (the same as Restore on Home). Otherwise the account is added beside the ones above and used from now on; Use switches back any time. Wallets imported one by one with their own key stay apart; signing in with an old arcade's @tag and password (Wallet → Accounts) brings those too. In a browser your words go to this arcade only: do it on a computer you trust, since browser extensions can read what a page shows.

          Look

          Themes are apps from the App Store's Themes category. One changes how this window looks and is laid out (an application window with menus, or a desktop with windows and a taskbar), never what it does: every screen is still this one's. It is checked before it is worn: its text must be readable, and its style can only reach its own frame. This window keeps its own choice; the desktop app and each browser choose for themselves.

          Read the code before it runs here: every release's code travels with it, as the repository @arcade/arcade-v1 that every arcade keeps.

          Off unless you turn it on. Releases come from the Arcade V1 network itself: every arcade keeps the releases signed with Strawberry's release key and hands them to the arcades it is linked to, so no website is involved. When on, this arcade installs the newest one it holds by itself (it looks every 10 minutes): the release is checked against its signed record, the old programs are kept beside the new ones (as .prev), and the service restarts cleanly. Your wallet, @handle, messages and chains stay as they are. If the app window is open, open it again after an update to load the new version.

              Use this arcade from a browser

              This same window, with every tab, opens in a web browser: on this computer, or on another one (a laptop) through an SSH tunnel. Nothing new is opened to the network: the arcade still answers only this computer, and the tunnel brings the other computer's browser here. You're using it in a browser now.

              1. On another computer, open the tunnel in a terminal there and leave it running:
                …
                It asks for this computer's login password (or uses your SSH key). The port must be the same on both ends.
              2. Open the link in that computer's browser (or in a browser here, without a tunnel):
                hidden
                The link holds this arcade's key. Anyone with the link and a way in can do what this app does, wallet included, so treat it like your wallet's words. Run arcade web in a terminal here for the same link.
              3. Afterwards the plain address http://127.0.0.1:8420/ui/ works in that browser, until this arcade restarts (an update, a reboot). Then the key changes: come back here, or run arcade web, for the new link.

              On your home network the operator can instead put a password-protected entrance in front of the arcade (an https address on this computer, for home-network addresses only), so another computer there needs no tunnel: just that address and the password. The tunnel above works from anywhere.
